body.statement: At \(a=q_0=e_0=e_1=1/2\), \((p_0,p_1)=(3/10,4/5)\), and \(G=B=C=2\), the sharp upper endpoint is \(F_+(P)=61/80\), the first Proposition 3 component is \(V_1^+=25/32\), the second is \(V_2^+=49/64\), and therefore \(V^+-F_+(P)=1/320>0\). The same strict ordering persists on a relative neighborhood inside \(\mathcal M_\eta\) for every \(\eta<1/5\).
body.justification: An exact rational witness certifies that compatibility has non-negligible empirical content beyond the published relaxations.
body.gap: The numerical examples in Tan (2025) do not supply this exact active-product strictness certificate.
body.consumer: It is a regression test for software implementing both the sharp and conservative binary endpoints.
body.proof_tex:
At the displayed law, the envelope calculations are exact:
\[
 U_2(3/10)=3/5,\quad U_2(4/5)=9/10,\quad
 r^+=(9/20,17/20),\quad t^+=(29/40,37/40),\quad
 (h^-,h^+)=(1/4,3/4).
\]
Because \(t_0^+<t_1^+\), the maximizing covariate weight is \(h^-\).  Hence
\[
 F_+(P)=\frac12\frac{(9/20+17/20)}2
 +\frac12\left\{\frac14\frac{29}{40}+\frac34\frac{37}{40}\right\}
 =\frac{13}{40}+\frac7{16}=\frac{61}{80}.
\]

We next certify the first program without numerical optimization.  For \(K=2\),
\[
 z_0(k)=k/2,\qquad z_1(k)=2-k,\qquad
 T_2(z,c)\geq z/2+c/2,\quad T_2(z,c)\geq2z-c.
\]
Use the first lower affine piece at \(z_0\) and the second at \(z_1\).  The coefficient of each \(k_\ell\) in the resulting lower bound is \(q_\ell(1-9r_\ell^+)/4<0\), and the coefficient of the common \(c\) is
\[
 \sum_\ell q_\ell\{(1-r_\ell^+)/2-r_\ell^+\}
 =\frac12-\frac32\frac{13}{20}<0.
\]
Thus the lower bound is minimized at \(k_0=k_1=c=1\), where the selected affine pieces are active and the bound is attained.  Its value is
\[
 \sum_\ell q_\ell\left(\frac34+\frac{r_\ell^+}{4}\right)
 =\frac34+\frac{13}{80}=\frac{73}{80}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 V_1^+=\frac{13}{40}+\frac12\frac{73}{80}=\frac{25}{32}.
\]

For the second program, write \(A_\ell=A_\ell(c_\ell)\) and \(D_\ell=D_\ell(k_\ell,c_\ell)\).  Since
\[
 R_2(D_0,D_1)\geq\frac14D_0+\frac34D_1,
\]
every feasible value is at least
\[
 \left(\frac14A_0+\frac18D_0\right)
 +\left(\frac14A_1+\frac38D_1\right).
\]
The general inequalities in the conservative-frontier proof give \(A_1\geq17/20\) and \(D_1\geq37/40\), simultaneously attained at \(c_1=k_1=1\).  The second parenthesis is therefore at least \(179/320\).

For stratum zero, direct calculation with
\[
 H(x,c)=\max\{3x/2-c/2,,3x/4+c/4\}
\]
gives \(A_0(c)=9/20+c/40\).  Minimizing \(D_0(k,c)\) over \(k\in[0,1]\) gives
\[
 \min_kD_0(k,c)=
 \begin{cases}
 9/10-7c/20,&0\leq c\leq1/2,\\
 57/80+c/40,&1/2\leq c\leq1.
 \end{cases}
\]
To verify this display, note that \(z_1(k)\geq c\), while the active piece at \(z_0(k)=k/2\) changes at \(k=2c\); the objective decreases up to that point and increases afterward when \(c\leq1/2\), whereas for \(c\geq1/2\) it decreases through \(k=1\).  Therefore
\[
 2A_0(c)+D_0(k,c)\geq\frac{33}{20},
\]
with equality at \(c_0=1/2,k_0=1\).  The first parenthesis is at least \(33/160\).  At these four thresholds, \((D_0,D_1)=(29/40,37/40)\), so the displayed face \(h=1/4\) of \(R_2\) is active.  Hence the lower bound is attained and
\[
 V_2^+=\frac{33}{160}+\frac{179}{320}=\frac{49}{64}.
\]
Thus \(V^+=49/64\) and
\[
 V^+-F_+(P)=\frac{49}{64}-\frac{61}{80}=\frac1{320}>0.
\]
Moreover, \(V_1^+-V_2^+=1/64>0\), so the exact ordering is
\[
 F_+(P)<V_2^+=V^+<V_1^+.
\]

Finally, every envelope and check-transform is continuous.  Each conservative value is the minimum of a jointly continuous function over a fixed compact cube, so the elementary inequality
\[
 \left|\min_u g(x,u)-\min_u g(x',u)\right|
 \leq\sup_u|g(x,u)-g(x',u)|
\]
shows that \(V_1^+\) and \(V_2^+\) are continuous in the primitive probabilities and sensitivity constants.  The compact sharp formula is continuous as well.  Both strict gaps in the last ordering therefore persist on a relative neighborhood.  At the witness the smallest primitive probability or complement is \(1/5\); hence, for every \(\eta<1/5\), that neighborhood can be chosen inside \(\mathcal M_\eta\).
